newsitem.title: USA: PairGain slumps on earnings momentum fears.
newsitem.headline: PairGain slumps on earnings momentum fears.

text.p: Shares of PairGain Technologies Inc slumped over 16 percent Thursday on fears the communications innovator may have difficulty maintaining earnings growth momentum.
PairGain was off 4-7/8 to 25 in heavy afternoon trading on Nasdaq, with more than 11 million shares changing hands.

The fall came despite strong first quarter earnings, released yesterday. PairGain posted operating profits of $0.19 a share, before charges, on revenues of $70.7 million, beating the First Call consensus estimate of $0.17 a share.
In the comparable year-ago quarter the company earned $0.09 a share on revenues of $40.5 million.
Analysts said investors sold off the shares today because receivables during the first quarter rose to $11 million.

"They were in the last month of the quarter and, realizing they were not going to meet their revenue projection, they extended terms to their customers to entice them to order now," said Michael Davies, an analyst at Utendahl Capital Partners. "It shows you that they struggled hard to reach their revenue number."

PairGain is the dominant company in digital subscriber line-based systems that allow firms with private networks to send data, video and voice over ordinary telephone lines. The company has strong relationships with the regional Bells, which use PairGain products to speed the flow of information over copper phone lines rather than upgrade to more expensive fibre optics lines. Demand for PairGain products has blossomed with the explosive growth of the Internet.
Davies said the perception among investors was that the company may have enticed customers who would normally have bought in the second quarter to buy in the first quarter.
"That's a harbinger of the sustainability of that revenue growth," he said.

Nevertheless, Davies increased his second quarter earnings estimate for PairGain to $0.19 a share from $0.18 and is upbeat on the future of the company. He expects revenues of $320 million in fiscal 1997 and $420 million in 1998, up from $205 million in 1996.
Davies was not alone in raising his earnings estimate. Both Lehman Brothers and Hambrecht & Quist increased their estimates for PairGain and made positive comments on the company yesterday.
